text: The building across the street has forty windows.
I know every one of them by heart.
Four dances alone. Twelve talks to her cat. Thirty cries on Sundays.
I don't sleep much. So I watch.
Nobody ever looks up.
Window nine had been dark for a year.
On Tuesday, at eleven, the light came on.
I watched a man kill a woman. Every second of it.
The police found nothing. No body. No blood. No woman.
The apartment had been empty for a year. They said I dreamed it.
On Wednesday, at eleven... he killed her again.
Same second. Same arm. Same silent scream.
People don't die the same way twice.
So I did the one thing a watcher never does.
I crossed the street.
There was no murder. Just a lamp... a sheet... and two paper dolls.
It was never a crime. It was a show.
And for the first time, I saw my own window from the other side.
Someone was standing in it.
He doesn't kill the women in the windows.
He kills the women who watch.
I had ninety seconds. Maybe less.
He'd shown me how it works. A light. A sheet. Something for the eye to believe.
So I gave him a show.
They found forty paper dolls in his room. One for every window.
One of them was holding binoculars.
I don't watch the windows anymore.
Mostly.
Be honest... would you have crossed the street?
